item.text: The lookup currently converts a valid ID of `0` and the absence of any ID into the same result. It also accepts a nonnumeric `ps-` key in the fallback path. I’m adding regression cases for those boundaries before changing the lookup and its public bookmark caller.

/bin/bash -lc "cat >> .codex-role-output/checkpoint.md <<'EOF'

Root cause: fallback "'`lastLocalID?.ID || 0` collapses missing data and legitimate ID 0. Both lookup loops accept every `ps-` key and convert suffixes with `Number`, so malformed suffixes can yield NaN or spuriously win. `resumeSession` requires a numeric localID and public bookmark hook passes the result directly. Hypothesis: strict numeric-key filtering plus a null sentinel, with a caller guard, restores the intended distinction. Regression tests added; baseline run pending.
EOF'

item.text:
Updated `getLastPersistedLocalID` to return `null` when no valid ID is found, ignore keys without a numeric suffix, and preserve valid ID `0`. The public bookmark hook now calls `resumeSession` only when an ID exists.

The regression tests pass (13/13), and `git diff --check` passes. The Drive type check remains blocked by an unrelated OpenPGP type mismatch in `packages/crypto/lib/worker/api.ts:579`; I recorded the command and error in [.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md).
